name: אינטגרל מסוים של sin³(x) – בעזרת sin²=1−cos² (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find

\( \displaystyle \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}}\, d{{CT:3}} = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Write \(\sin^3 x=\sin x\cdot\sin^2 x\), integrate by parts, solve the resulting equation for the integral, and substitute the limits.
Step 1 — Rewriting the integrand
To solve this problem we will have to express {{CT:4}} in a simpler way using some trigonometric identities
Pythagorean identity: \( \sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1 \)
Step 2 — Integration by parts
Now, recall that if \(u\) and \(v\) are both functions of \(x\) then

\[ \int u\, dv = uv - \int v\, du. \]

So, let \(u = {{CT:5}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:6}}\, d{{CT:3}}\). Then \(du = {{CT:7}}\, d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:8}}\). So,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:2}}\, d{{CT:3}} &= \int u\, dv \\ &= uv - \int v\, du \\ &= [{{CT:5}}][{{CT:8}}] - \int [{{CT:8}}][{{CT:7}}d{{CT:3}}] +c \\ &= {{CT:9}} - \int {{CT:10}}d{{CT:3}} +c \\ &= {{CT:9}} + 2\int {{CT:6}}[{{CT:11}}] d{{CT:3}} +c \\ &= {{CT:9}} + 2\int {{CT:12}} d{{CT:3}} +c \end{aligned} \]

Step 3 — Solving for the integral
Hence,

\[ 3\int {{CT:2}}\, d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:9}} + 2\int {{CT:6}}\, d{{CT:3}} +c \]

And so,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:2}}\, d{{CT:3}} &= {{CT:13}}+ {{CT:14}} + \frac{c}{3} \\ &= {{CT:15}} + \frac{c}{3}. \end{aligned} \]

Step 4 — Substituting the limits
Then

\[ \begin{aligned} \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}}\, d{{CT:3}} &= F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\ &= {{CT:16}} - \left[{{CT:17}}\right] \\ &= {{CT:18}} \end{aligned} \]
